title: The fourteen video pages still contradict the video design they were corrected by
goal: The video design study settled how a video document looks in this app, and the fourteen video clickthrough pages still draw the old answer: no layers list in the dock, and a clip whose start and end are typed into a grid of number boxes. Anyone opening those pages reads a design the study says is wrong. Bring the pages into line so the study and the pages say one thing.
notes:
Found while finishing the video design pass on 2026-09-20. Evidence, run from the repo root:

  $ for f in docs/design/mocks/pages/video*.html; do echo "$(grep -c 'ttl">Layers' $f) $(basename $f)"; done

Only video-shell draws it. video-entry-wt.html line 148 still carries the comment "no Layers group here: the timeline below IS the layer list" and line 342 still tells the reader "there is no separate Layers panel to manage", which is exactly what UX-PATTERNS D18 now forbids.

The 2026-09-19 pass corrected video.html's caption (it says out loud that removing Layers was wrong) and renamed rows on fifteen pages, but putting the GROUP back is a change to fourteen laid-out docks and the scripts that drive them, so it was left. video-surface.md §7 now says so rather than claiming it was done.

Second half, same pages: video-entry-wt.html lines 156-166 draw the Clip section as a four box grid (In, Out, Speed, Vol) with an explaining paragraph under it. video-surface.md §2 settles that time is never a number in the panel (in, out, duration and speed are dragged on the strip, and an exact number opens the way Position and Size opens, which is worth 130 points every time), and §5 settles that a section needing a paragraph inside it is misnamed. The settled Clip section is Reads, Volume, Speed as three rows. Careful with the walkthrough script: step data-set writes #pOut, so removing that field without touching the step breaks the walk.
acceptance: Every page under docs/design/mocks/pages/video*.html shows the Layers group in its dock, listing the same layers as its timeline rows, in the same order, with the same icons
No video page puts a clip's in, out or duration in the panel as a field: that is set by dragging, and the exact number opens the way Position and Size opens
No video page needs a paragraph inside a panel section to explain what the section is for
Every mock gate stays green (reserved, a11y, selection, states, elevation, easing, shortcuts) and every page still renders and still walks its walkthrough end to end

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The correction itself holds: a video document carries layers that never occupy time (background, adjustment, matte, component master), and with Layers deleted those have no row anywhere, so the mocks' 'the timeline IS the layer list' was wrong on its own terms. Build it. (2) Cheapest honest version: one dgrp data-grp=layers data-gh=sm at the TOP of each dock (132px, the canonical video-shell size) plus a Layers rail tab, NOT a restructure of each page's Properties group into per-selection top-level groups the way video-shell draws them. That second change has no mandate in the acceptance and would rewrite fourteen docks for no user-visible gain; left out deliberately. (3) A Layers group that never lights up when you click a clip would be decoration, so every walkthrough step that selects a clip now also selects its row: data-select clears .sel across .lrow, so the two views cannot disagree. (4) Risk found and handled: removing #pOut etc. breaks any step whose data-set writes it; every such step was rewritten in the same pass.

Built and verified in a real browser (chrome devtools on the dev server), not by grep. All 15 video* pages: Layers is the FIRST group of every visible dock, its rows match the strip one for one in name, order and icon, no dock overflows, every walkthrough runs to its last step and resets, and no page throws a JS error or scrolls horizontally. Seven walkthroughs cover 59 steps between them. Five pages build their strip from a list in JS (video, video-motion, video-compositing, video-audio, video-captions) and their Layers group is now built from that SAME list, so the two cannot drift. Selection is wired both ways on every page that has a selection.

Adversarial review AFTER building, on the pages themselves. (1) Found a real defect I had just introduced: the dock's Panels footer is generated from the groups, so adding Layers to fourteen docks also added a switch that turns Layers OFF, which D18 says nothing may do and which the app cannot do (PanelSectionVisibility.optionalSections deliberately does not list Layers). Fixed in shared/components/dock.js: a group marked data-required, or any data-grp=layers, is still LISTED (the list answers 'which panes do I have') but carries no switch and says why on hover. Verified: clicking Layers in the Panels menu does nothing, clicking Library still hides it. Documented on pages/panes-panels.html, which is that mechanism's own page. This is wider than the video pages: 13 sample pages across the study re-checked, all clean, all gates green. (2) On video-transition-wt nothing in Layers ever lights up, because a cut is not a layer, and a group that never responds reads as broken. Rather than fake a selection I gave the page a caption saying what the list is for there (the eye beside voice-over is how you audition a cut without the music). (3) video-title-wt drew a title layer and a component instance as two clips sharing ONE row called 'Lower third' - a track model. Split into two rows, one per layer, and the title row now renames itself from its own words in both views.

Judgment calls, so a later pass does not undo them by accident. (a) What counts as 'a number box': a .grid2 of boxed .field elements is out everywhere; an .irow with a way in (the Volume stepper, a transition's Length select) is the shape video-shell and UX-PATTERNS D-rules already bless, so it stays. A transition's length and a dip's Hold on black are therefore kept - they are also not a CLIP's in, out or duration, which is what the acceptance names. Written up in the audit's rough so the user can disagree in one click. (b) Left rough, not filed: the library-scope explainer paragraphs (a shared idiom on 7 pages, mostly non-video) and the history-sheet footers are not paragraphs inside a panel SECTION explaining what the section is for, so they stayed. (c) Left rough, not filed: video-transition-wt's Black clip is drawn as its own clip object where video-surface.md §2 says a dip is an outline inside each clip's own time. Out of this task's acceptance and it would rewrite the page's central mechanic. (d) I deliberately did NOT restructure the fourteen docks into video-shell's per-selection top-level groups (Clip/Appearance/Motion instead of one Properties group holding sections). No acceptance item asks for it and it is fourteen laid-out docks for no user-visible gain. (e) Icons were unified with video-shell while matching them across the two views: a video clip is ic-film (was ic-image), an audio layer is ic-waveform (was ic-audio).

Docs updated so the pages and the study now agree in writing too: video-surface.md §7 says the Layers row is done rather than filed, §5 records what was applied; UX-PATTERNS D18 gains a paragraph saying the fourteen conform and how (one list builds both views where the strip is scripted). Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-22-video-layers.json with two real browser screenshots. The panel-room cost was folded into the open task appearance-is-below-the-fold-again-because-the-p rather than filed as its own.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Correction on my own last act: I asked for a full walk sweep on the grounds that shared/components/dock.js changed. That was the wrong call and I am saying so rather than leaving it to look deliberate. The walk set drives the built app; docs/design/mocks/ is HTML on the design dashboard and no walk touches it. Nothing under Sources/ changed in this task, so the sweep has nothing to find here. Asking is not starting and four requests were already pending, so it costs the loop nothing extra, but the next runner should not read this as evidence the sweep was needed.

All fifteen docs/design/mocks/pages/video*.html pages now open Layers as the first group of every dock, listing the same rows as the strip in the same order with the same icons, with selection wired both ways; the five pages that script their strip build the Layers group from that same list so they cannot drift. Every grid of boxed in/out/duration fields is gone (a clip's section is Reads, Volume, Speed) and so is every paragraph inside a panel section explaining what the section was for. Six leftover track-model errors fixed along the way (V1 -> Story, a title and a component sharing one row, Source/Retimed drawn as timeline rows, video-captions having no row for its recording, a permanent empty voice-over track, and video-compositing calling its layers two different things). Also fixed a defect this pass introduced: the dock's Panels footer offered a switch that turned Layers off, which D18 forbids; a required pane is now listed without a switch (shared/components/dock.js + dock.css, documented on panes-panels.html). Verified in a real browser on the dev server: 15/15 pages render Layers first in every dock, no dock overflows, no horizontal overflow, seven walkthroughs run all 59 steps and reset, no JS errors. All eight mock gates green; Scripts/test.sh green (8952 tests in 713 suites). Docs brought in line: video-surface.md §5 and §7, UX-PATTERNS D18. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-22-video-layers.json with two real screenshots. Committed and pushed as 7cb506b1.
